text: Judy Reyes, born November 5, 1967, in the Bronx, New York City, to Dominican immigrants, is an American actress, model, and producer best known for her roles as Carla Espinosa on the NBC/ABC medical comedy series Scrubs (2001–2009), as Zoila Diaz in the Lifetime comedy-drama Devious Maids (2013–2016), as Annalise "Quiet Ann" Zayas in the TNT crime comedy-drama Claws (2017–2022), and as Selena Soto in the ABC crime drama series High Potential (2024–). She also appeared in the films All Together Now (2020), Smile (2022), and Birth/Rebirth (2023), for which she received an Independent Spirit Award for Best Lead Performance nomination. Reyes has three sisters, including a fraternal twin sister named Joselin Reyes, who played a paramedic on Law & Order: Special Victims Unit. She grew up on Bainbridge Avenue from the age of 13 to 25–26 and attended Hunter College in Manhattan, where she began her acting career. In the early 1990s, she began her television career with guest starring roles in shows like Law & Order, NYPD Blue, and The Sopranos, and had a recurring role in Oz as Tina Rivera. She is best known for her portrayal of nurse Carla Espinosa on Scrubs from 2001 to 2009 and has starred in several made-for-television movies for Lifetime, including Little Girl Lost: The Delimar Vera Story (2008) and The Pregnancy Project (2012). After leaving Scrubs, she guest-starred in Castle, Medium, Off the Map, and Law & Order: Special Victims Unit. In 2011, she starred in the independent drama Gun Hill Road, set in the Bronx, which refers to a real-life street intersecting Bainbridge Avenue where she grew up; the film premiered at the Sundance Film Festival. She also had small supporting roles in films such as Went to Coney Island on a Mission from God... Be Back by Five (1998), Bringing Out the Dead (1999), Washington Heights (2002), and Dirty (2005). In 2012, she was cast as series regular Zoila Diaz in the ABC comedy-drama pilot Devious Maids, created by Marc Cherry; the series was not picked up by ABC but was ordered by Lifetime for thirteen episodes on June 22, 2012, and premiered on June 23, 2013, with its finale airing on August 8, 2016. Two weeks after the show's cancellation, she was cast opposite Niecy Nash in Claws as Annalise "Quiet Ann" Zayas, which premiered on June 11, 2017, and ended in 2022 after four seasons. She also had recurring roles as Dina Milagro in Jane the Virgin (2015–2019) and as Ramona in One Day at a Time (2017–2020). In 2018, she played Eva, executive producer of media conglomerate Waystar Royco's ATN news channel, in the HBO drama Succession. She also had recurring roles in Search Party and Better Things and guest starred on Black-ish. In 2022, she guest-starred in season 3 of Batwoman as Kiki Roulette, who was responsible for building Joker's joy buzzer. Reyes starred in the independent films My Name Is David (2015) and Girl Flu (2016) and had a supporting role in The Circle (2017). She received an Imagen Award for Best Actress - Drama (Television) for her performance in the 2021 made-for-television film Torn from Her Arms. She appeared opposite her One Day at a Time co-star Justina Machado in the 2020 drama film All Together Now. In 2022, she had a supporting role in the supernatural horror film Smile, which was a box office success, grossing over $217 million worldwide. The following year, she played the leading role in the psychological horror film Birth/Rebirth, which premiered at the Sundance Film Festival and received positive reviews; she received an Independent Spirit Award for Best Lead Performance nomination. In 2023, she had a recurring role in the horror-comedy series The Horror of Dolores Roach, appearing again opposite Justina Machado. Reyes appeared as the mother of the lead character in the romantic drama film Turtles All the Way Down, based on the 2017 novel by John Green. She was also cast opposite Kaitlin Olson in a series regular role in the ABC comedy-drama series High Potential, based on the French series HPI. As of May 2002, Reyes was married to cinematographer Edwin Figueroa. She is currently in a relationship with director George Valencia, and together they founded the non-profit Sound of GOL Foundation!, a "recreational past time charity for young girls."
